Still unbacked: the daily CTR-trend signal described in the FAQ, model section and README could not fire on a realistic daily export (README 'Known gaps' said so, the page did not); the page did not say that column names are from memory and unchecked against a real export (README:28, VENTURE.yaml:44 do). evidence.domain: Unchanged method on arrival: pooled cross-sectional medians across campaign types (calc.mjs:279-280), no CPM, uncited thresholds (now labelled rules of thumb in README). After this PR the time-based signal on daily exports follows the practitioner diagnosis (the same ad's CTR decline over its own days) without a frequency gate the data cannot reach, and states the honest upper bound on period frequency. Segmentation and CPM remain open. 2.

defects.what: On arrival, a realistic daily export (per-day frequency ~1.2) still never triggered the CTR-trend fatigue signal, because it is gated on frequency >= 3; the fix PR only documented it.
Fatigue compares ads with one median pooled across campaign types, so retargeting dominates flags; CPM is not computed.
Page did not disclose (as README and VENTURE.yaml do) that column names are from memory and unchecked against a real export.
Thresholds (3, 0.8x, 1.25x, -25%) remain unsourced rules of thumb.
`clicks` alias falls back to bare 'clicks' (Clicks (all) taken as link clicks); matched CTR column never read; `ignored` never incremented.

verdict: Of the seven defects the 2026-11-13 audit counted fixed by PR #15600, two were closed (tab-file decimal commas, the four surviving threshold mutants), two were partly addressed, and three were open, including the only high one: PR #15600 wrote the daily-frequency defect into the README instead of fixing it. The standard-path arithmetic still matches Meta's definitions on all 13 sample ads, and all six seeded mutants are now caught. On arrival it does not meet the bar: correctness and claims are 2 because the advertised daily CTR-trend signal could not fire on a real daily export. This PR fixes that (daily exports flag a CTR fall on its own, with the upper bound on period frequency stated) and adds the page's missing unverified-columns disclosure; scores are not raised for those fixes. Pooled medians and missing CPM remain the main domain gap.
